subject: stf
title: STF.------RT.ALGN.
description: Partial-label diagram in JR-6 (Jazz-Rock). The prose immediately above identifies the structural target: 'the emergence of jazz-rock can be looked at as a positive factor for both jazz and rock musicians, yet for different reasons. Because if jazz-rock would be the form that would lead jazz musicians back into national acceptance, it would also be a vehicle to legitimize rock music — as a serious art form worthy of the critical defining community — and a form that — after its transfer shift completion — functioned in accordance to the dictates of the western defining community as well (thus securing the next arena for spectacle-diversion-transfer progressionalism).' STF (source transfer) crossed with RT-ALGN (reality alignment). STF sits at the title-axis subject; RT-ALGN at upper-center as partner-axis with RT-ALGN labeled below the title. Only four nodes are labeled in the diagram: RT-ALGN at upper-center-left, (R)DOC (the reality of documentation) at upper-center, APP-RDEF (applied redefinitions) at upper-right, and ALT-F (alternative functionalism) at center-right. Eight further dots are unlabeled, among them the lower end of the main line from RT-ALGN; no STF label or subject-arrow is drawn. (R)DOC branches from the main line, ALT-F from (R)DOC's line, and APP-RDEF from ALT-F's line; the unlabeled dots form the rest of the branching structure. Structural argument: the partial-label form is structurally meaningful — the four labeled outputs (RT-ALGN, (R)DOC, APP-RDEF, ALT-F) name the western-defining-community's working channels that jazz-rock's transfer-shift completion enters, while the unlabeled internal junctions stand for the *unspecified* working positions the form passes through on its way to securing the spectacle-diversion-transfer progressionalism the prose names. The diagram structurally claims that the form's source transfer reaches the partner-axis's reality-alignment along the main line, with the labeled (R)DOC → ALT-F → APP-RDEF chain off it, through an otherwise unspecified tree. The form's actual working content at the unlabeled internal nodes never receives names because the western definers do not name them — they receive the form only at the four labeled outputs.
